issues.description: The task, tests, and reference solution expect a helper named make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None, but the template defines a different function name create_y_state(circ, q, p). The template's stub even raises NotImplementedError("make_y_state is not implemented."), which confirms the intended name is make_y_state. This naming mismatch will break automated tests and confuses students implementing the function because the starter code does not expose the name the problem statement asks for.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template and problem wording consistent by renaming the template stub create_y_state to make_y_state with the signature make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Alternatively add a thin wrapper in the template: def make_y_state(circ, q, p): return create_y_state(circ, q, p). Update the stub's NotImplementedError message and docstring to reference make_y_state so tests and task descriptions match the code.
